rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.e1: Defense: let us think from White's side, with White to move. Game Rummenige × Whitewing, Lichess 2020. The black queen on f5 gives check to your king on h3.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.e2: Before attacking, ask what your opponent threatens. Here there are two things: the check and the capture of your queen on d5, which the queen on f5 also attacks.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.p: Find the move that blocks the check and saves your queen.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.certo: The bishop goes to g4 and blocks the check. It also pins the black queen: behind it, on the same diagonal, is the king on d7. The queen can no longer capture yours.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the bishop to g4: it blocks the check and pins the black queen to the king on d7.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.err.d5f5.1: Your queen captures the queen on f5, but it was defended by the knight on d6.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.err.d5f5.2: The knight recaptures your queen. Black keeps an extra rook and wins.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.err.d5f5.3: Back to the position: look for the move that blocks the check and saves your queen.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.err.g3g4.1: The pawn goes to g4 and blocks the check, but your queen on d5 is still attacked.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.err.g3g4.2: The black queen captures your queen. The bishop on f3 recaptures, and Black keeps an extra rook.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.err.g3g4.3: Back to the position: look for the move that blocks the check and saves your queen.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.fora: The king gets out of check, but your queen on d5 is still attacked. Look for the move that deals with both threats.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: your queen on d5 is also attacked.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.l1: The black queen is pinned and attacked, with no way to save itself. All it can do is capture the bishop, to take at least one piece.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.l2: The queen captures the bishop on g4 with check.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.l3: Your king recaptures the queen. White gave up the bishop and won the queen.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex1.l4: This is the defensive move. In positions like this, before attacking, ask what your opponent threatens. Here there were two threats, and a single move stopped both.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.e1: Defense: now with Black, in the Game jcphillips8 × richardregueiro, Lichess 2023. Your king is in the center, on e5, and the white rooks and queen are closing in on it.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.e2: White threatens to give mate with the rooks and the queen. Before thinking about your own attack, look for the move that stops this threat. Look at the g-file: the queen on g6 stands in front of the white king on g2.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.p: Find the move that stops the mating threat.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.certo: The rook goes to g7 and attacks the queen. The queen is pinned: if it leaves the g-file, it leaves the king on g2 in check.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the rook to g7: it attacks the queen, pinned to the king on g2 along the g-file.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.err.a4a3.1: The pawn advances to become a queen, but White's threat is still there.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.err.a4a3.2: The queen gives check on f5 and then captures your bishop on f4. White wins.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.err.a4a3.3: Back to the position: the white queen is on the g-file, in front of its own king. Attack it along that file.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.err.e5d4.1: The king runs to d4, but leaves the pawn on f6 undefended.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.err.e5d4.2: The queen captures the pawn on f6 with check and then your bishop on f4. White wins.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.err.e5d4.3: Back to the position: the white queen is on the g-file, in front of its own king. Attack it along that file.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not stop White's threat. Look at the g-file, between the white queen and the king on g2.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the white queen is on the g-file, in front of the king.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.l1: The queen cannot leave the g-file. White still gives one check before losing it.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook gives check on h5: White looks for one more move with check before giving up the queen.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.l3: Your king goes to d4, away from the rooks.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.l4: The queen is still attacked and pinned. It captures the rook on g7, to take at least one piece.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.l5: Your rook on a7 recaptures with check. Black gave up the rook and won the queen.
rot.defensiveMove.ideia.ex2.l6: In positions like this, before thinking about your own attack, look for your opponent's threat. Sometimes the move that stops it also wins material.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.ganhaTempo.1: Defense: now with White, in the Game AleksandrVuktyl × Nadtkins, Lichess 2023. The black queen on b6 gives check to your king on g1, and the black bishop on e5 is attacked by the pawn on f4.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.ganhaTempo.2: Stepping the king to h1 looks natural, but it gives Black the time to save the bishop. There are moves that block the check. Which of them does more?
rot.defensiveMove.demos.ganhaTempo.3: The bishop on g3 goes to f2. It blocks the check and attacks the queen on b6.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.ganhaTempo.4: The queen gets out of the attack and goes to c7, where it defends the bishop. Black spent the move the bishop needed to escape.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.ganhaTempo.5: The pawn captures the bishop on e5. Black can only win back the pawn, and White wins a piece.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.ganhaTempo.6: In positions like this, among the moves that block the check, look for the one that attacks: your opponent spends the move saving the piece, and you gain time.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.corredor.1: Defense: White again, in the Game Duckies × isin1966, Lichess 2021. There is no check. Before attacking, ask what Black threatens.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.corredor.2: They threaten mate on your back rank: the queen gives check on a1, and the bishop on f4 covers h2, your king's only escape square.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.corredor.3: Your queen captures the bishop on f4. It wins a piece and opens the h2 square for the king.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.corredor.4: The black queen gives the check on a1 anyway, looking for mate.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.corredor.5: The king escapes to h2, and the mate is gone. Your queen is also attacking the knight on c7.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.corredor.6: In positions like this, the defense can be a capture: removing the piece that was helping the mate also stops the threat.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.1: Defense: now with Black, in the Game RIBANT × sophiesoutrenon, Lichess 2015. White threatens to capture your rook on d8 with mate. Defending looks natural.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.2: Before defending, look at the checks you have. Is any of them worth more than the defense?
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.p: Find the strongest move for Black.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.certo: Your queen captures the bishop on d1 with check.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.revela: The move is the queen to d1: it captures the bishop with check.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.err.d8d6: The rook captures the rook on d6 and removes the threat on d8.
The queen gives check on e8. The rook goes back to d8 to block, and the queen captures it with mate.
Defending was not enough: White had checks. Back to the position: calculate your checks.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.err.a4c3: The knight gives check to the king on b1.
The king goes to b2 and attacks the knight. The mate threat on d8 is still there.
Back to the position: look for the check that does not leave the threat standing.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.3: The king on b1 has no free square, and the check will have to be dealt with by the rook on d6.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.4: The rook on d6 recaptures the queen and leaves the d-file open for your rook on d8.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.5: Your rook recaptures with mate: the king on b1 has no square, and the back rank belongs to the rook.
rot.defensiveMove.demos.excecao.6: In positions like this, before defending, look at the checks you have. If one of them forces mate or wins material, it comes before the defense.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.valeAqui.enunc: Black threatens mate on g2 with the queen. Defending g2 at once, with the rook or the queen, looks natural. Does it work here? Play as White.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.valeAqui.fim: First the queen captured the rook on f8 with check. Had the king taken it, a rook would check on d8 and mate on e8. After the king went to h7, the rook on d2 stopped the mate on g2.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.valeAqui.err.d: The rook defends g2, but the knight on f6 goes to e4 and attacks the rook and your queen at the same time. Before defending, look for a move with check.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.valeAqui.err.c: The queen defends g2, but leaves the rook on f8 alone, and Black has the advantage. Before defending, look for a move with check.
The queen captures the pawn on f7, but the mate on g2 is still there. Now stop that threat.
The rook on e1 covers g2, but the black queen captures it, and your king cannot escape. Hold g2 with the other rook.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.cobrir.enuncia: Now with Black. The white queen on e5 gives check to your king on g7. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.cobrir.fim: The pawn on f6 blocked the check and attacked the queen, without trading queens. It went to f4, and the pawn on e5 attacked the queen and the knight on d4 at the same time: a pawn fork.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.cobrir.err.d8f: The queen blocks the check, but the queens are traded, and the game is level. Block the check without trading queens, and gain time.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.cobrir.err.g7h: The king gets out of check, but the knight on d4 goes to c6 and attacks your queen and the rook on b8. White wins material. Block the check.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.cobrir.err.g7g: The king gets out of check, but White gains time, and the game is level. Block the check with a move that attacks the queen.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.cobrir.err2.g6: The pawn attacks the queen, but it escapes, and Black loses the advantage. Look for the move that attacks the queen and the knight on d4 at the same time.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.tempo.enunciad: The black queen on b4 gives check to your king and also attacks the knight on a4. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.tempo.fim: The bishop went back to d2, blocked the check and attacked the queen. It captured the knight on a4, and your queen recaptured it: White won the queen for a knight.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.tempo.err.a4c3: The knight blocks the check, but the queen captures the pawn on b2 and then attacks the rook on a1. Black wins material. Block the check while attacking the queen.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.tempo.err.f3d2: The knight blocks the check, and the game is level. Look for the move that blocks the check and also attacks the queen.
rot.defensiveMove.pratica.tempo.err2.b2b: The pawn attacks the queen, but it escapes, and your knight on a4 is already lost. Recapture the queen now.
